Study hour (300h) = 105 contact hours (70 slots) + 2 hours final exam + 193 hours self-study

Interactive Classroom Teaching

1 slot =90'
info.description: This course equips learners with advanced English skills for academic, social, and professional communication. The course develops mastery of complex grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation while fostering critical and cross-cultural awareness. Students analyze and discuss global and ethical issues, comprehend extended spoken and written texts, and express opinions or arguments with fluency and accuracy. Emphasis is placed on essay writing, critical reading, and effective collaboration. Learners integrate technology and AI tools for research and self-assessment, promoting leadership, professionalism, and lifelong global engagement.
info.studentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible for doing all exercises, assignments, and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submitting them on time

- Use a laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Access the course website for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
info.note:
1) On-going assessment: 60%

2) Final Examination (FE): 40%

3) Final Result: 100%

4) Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, each part of final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10.

materials.materialDescription: SF: Skillful 3 - Reading and Writing, Macmillan (pdf)
TE: Teacher’s Edition and Lesson Planner
materials.author: Joan Saslow, Allen Ascher

clos.loDetails: Identify and explain complex English vocabulary, grammatical structures, and pronunciation patterns used in academic, social, and professional contexts.
Analyze and discuss global, cultural, and ethical issues presented in authentic texts and media, demonstrating cross-cultural awareness and critical understanding.
Comprehend and interpret main ideas, details, and speaker intentions in extended spoken texts on familiar and abstract topics.
Express opinions, present arguments, and participate in formal and informal discussions using appropriate tone, intonation, and fluent, connected speech.
Evaluate and synthesize information from various written genres to infer meaning, author’s purpose, and bias using advanced reading strategies.
Compose clear and coherent essays that demonstrate logical organization, precise vocabulary, and accurate use of complex grammatical structures.
Apply information technology and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to enhance research, collaboration, and language learning efficiently, ethically, and responsibly.
Work independently and collaboratively with accountability, demonstrating respect, leadership, professionalism, and ethical behavior in diverse academic and professional contexts.
Design and implement a personal learning plan using self-assessment, feedback, and technology to monitor progress and foster lifelong English learning and global engagement.

sessions.studentMaterials: Student's book and CD, Workbook, Online resource
sessions.studentTasks:
Group work, pair work, individual work

Step 1: Use ChatGPT to find information about gerunds and infinitives.

Step 2: Summarize the Key Points

Based on ChatGPT's answer, create a short summary in your own words, including:

- What is a gerund? What is an infinitive?

- When do we use gerunds vs. infinitives?

- A list of common verbs followed by gerunds or infinitives

Step 3: Create a Learning Product

You can choose one of the following formats to present your summary:

A simple written summary in Google Docs

A mini infographic using Canva or Google Slides

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Knowledge and skills in studied unit(s)
assessments.note:
In classroom
Combination of unit tests or progress tests and/or other activities

assessments.questionType: MC, multi response, matching, gap filling, completion; essay writing; open questions
assessments.noQuestion: 1. Listening: 25%Includes 2 parts, 20 questions.2. Reading: 25%Includes 2 articles; 20 questions.3. Writing: 25%Includes 250 words; 4-paragraph essay; type: opinion essay and advantage-disadvantage essay.4. Speaking: 25%Includes topics of units in the textbook.
assessments.note:
1. Listening:

20 questions; 2 audios; MCQ 4 options, gap filling, matching; level: B2; around 3-5 mins/audio; 2 times listening; ~25 minutes

2. Reading:

20 questions; 2 texts - 500-600 words/text; MCQ 4 options, gap filling, matching; level: B2; topic: 10 units in the textbook; 40 minutes

3. Writing:

250 words, 4-paragraph essays - one topic; type: opinion essay and advantage-disadvantage essay; level: B2; 40 minutes

4. Speaking:

individually; 7 mins per student

Part 1. Long Run (1 min prep, 2-3 mins to speak)

1 minute to prepare

2-3 minutes to speak

Part 2. Discussion Questions (3 mins)

5 discussion questions provided

Teacher selects 1-2 questions to ask

Questions may be shuffled
